# nwc-kit

> Small, security-focused Nostr Wallet Connect client for TypeScript. Implements the NIP-47 core with NIP-44 v2 encryption and authenticated wallet responses, so an application can spend through a constrained connection to an existing Lightning wallet. Not a wallet, custody layer, policy engine or invoice verifier.

Live demo and documentation: https://forgesworn.github.io/nwc-kit/
GitHub: https://github.com/forgesworn/nwc-kit
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@forgesworn/nwc-kit

ESM-only. Node 22+, browsers, Deno and Bun. No `node:` imports. One runtime dependency: `nostr-tools`. Two subpath exports: `@forgesworn/nwc-kit` (main), `@forgesworn/nwc-kit/extensions/05` (transaction history).

**All NIP-47 amount, balance and fee fields are integers in milli-satoshis.** Convert sats explicitly at the application boundary.

## Install

npm install @forgesworn/nwc-kit

## Subpath Exports

### @forgesworn/nwc-kit (main entry)

Classes:
- `new NwcClient(connectionUri, options?)` — options: `{ transport?, requestTimeoutMs?, infoTimeoutMs?, now? }`. Default request timeout 60000ms, info timeout 10000ms; both must be 100–300000ms
- `new NostrRelayTransport(pool?)` — default transport over `nostr-tools` `SimplePool`
- `NwcError` — `{ code: NwcErrorCode, message: string, walletCode?: string }`

NwcClient methods:
- `connect() → Promise<NwcCapabilities>` — fetches the signed kind-13194 info event, requires `nip44_v2`
- `payInvoice({ invoice, amount?, metadata? }, options?) → Promise<PayInvoiceResult>`
- `makeInvoice({ amount, description?, description_hash?, expiry?, metadata? }, options?) → Promise<NwcTransaction>`
- `lookupInvoice({ payment_hash? | invoice? }, options?) → Promise<NwcTransaction>` — exactly one of the two
- `getBalance(options?) → Promise<{ balance: number }>`
- `getInfo(options?) → Promise<GetInfoResult>`
- `close() → void` — cancels pending requests, zeroises owned key material
- `capabilities` — getter, `NwcCapabilities | undefined`
- `walletPubkey`, `clientPubkey`, `relays` — readonly

Request options: `{ signal?: AbortSignal, timeoutMs?: number }`

Functions:
- `inspectNwcConnection(uri) → NwcConnectionInfo` — `{ walletPubkey, relays, lud16? }`, never returns the secret

Constants:
- `NWC_INFO_KIND` — 13194
- `NWC_REQUEST_KIND` — 23194
- `NWC_RESPONSE_KIND` — 23195

Error codes (`NwcErrorCode`): INVALID_CONNECTION, CLIENT_CLOSED, INFO_UNAVAILABLE, UNSUPPORTED_ENCRYPTION, UNSUPPORTED_METHOD, UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION, INVALID_REQUEST, PUBLISH_FAILED, RESPONSE_TIMEOUT, REQUEST_ABORTED, INVALID_RESPONSE, WALLET_ERROR

Types: GetBalanceResult, GetInfoResult, LookupInvoiceParams, MakeInvoiceParams, NwcCapabilities, NwcClientOptions, NwcConnectionInfo, NwcCoreMethod, NwcErrorCode, NwcEvent, NwcFilter, NwcPublishResult, NwcRequestOptions, NwcSubscription, NwcTransaction, NwcTransport, PayInvoiceParams, PayInvoiceResult

### @forgesworn/nwc-kit/extensions/05

Draft NWC extension 05, transaction history. Isolated so the core export cannot depend on a draft.

- `new NwcTransactionHistoryClient(connectionUri, options?)` — extends `NwcClient`
- `listTransactions({ from?, until?, limit?, offset?, unpaid?, type? }, options?) → Promise<{ transactions: NwcTransaction[] }>`

An explicit `limit` is always sent, defaulting to 20 and capped at 20, because the extension advises clients to page by at most 20 and wallets otherwise apply a larger default of their own.

## Usage

```ts
import { NwcClient } from '@forgesworn/nwc-kit'
import { tryDecodeBolt11, verifyPreimage } from 'farrier-kit'

const client = new NwcClient(connectionUri)
try {
  const capabilities = await client.connect()
  if (!capabilities.methods.includes('pay_invoice')) throw new Error('cannot pay')

  const decoded = tryDecodeBolt11(invoice)
  if (!decoded || decoded.amountMsats === null) throw new Error('bad invoice')

  const result = await client.payInvoice({ invoice })
  if (!verifyPreimage(result.preimage, decoded.paymentHashHex)) {
    throw new Error('wallet response does not settle this invoice')
  }
} finally {
  client.close()
}
```

## Security Model

- The relay is untrusted. Subscription filters are performance hints, not authentication. Every response is shape-checked, signature-verified and matched to the live request before decryption.
- Wallet author, request reference, client recipient and result method are all checked before a result is trusted.
- A valid wallet event that does not reference the active request is treated as a possible relay replay and ignored.
- NIP-44 v2 is required. Legacy NIP-04 is refused.
- The NWC connection URI is a spending capability. The library never logs or returns it. `close()` zeroises the library-owned secret and conversation-key byte arrays; JavaScript strings cannot be erased, so the caller still owns the URI string.
- Once publication begins, timeout, abort, close and publish failure are **ambiguous payment outcomes**, never proof of non-payment. Reconcile the invoice before retrying; a blind retry can pay twice.
- Passing tests are not evidence that money settled. Verify the invoice before paying and verify the returned preimage against the invoice payment hash afterwards — `farrier-kit` does both.

## Not In Scope

Wallet or node implementation, custody, balances or subwallet management, forward secrecy beyond NIP-44, BOLT-11 / LNURL / L402 / Cashu / WebLN / fiat functionality, legacy NIP-04 interoperability, amount policy, user approval and settlement verification.
